messages:
aj: quick heads-up — ran a profiling pass on the continuous batcher during the 2pm traffic spike. seeing consistent queue oscillation where long requests (>=1024 tokens) sit behind bursts of short 8–64 token requests and then get a big KV-cache eviction spike :thinking_face:
aj: flame snapshot + concise stats: p50_queue_delay_short=2ms p95_short=9ms p95_long=210ms; kv_hit_rate_before=87% kv_hit_rate_after_spike=41%
aj: attaching short excerpt of the profiler logs we used:
```
[2026-03-17T14:05:12Z] batcher: formed batch(short=34,long=1) -> exec_kernel=fastpath_v2
[2026-03-17T14:05:12Z] runtime: kv_eviction(tenant=team-x, freed=18MB)
[2026-03-17T14:05:12Z] req: long(id=0xabc, tokens=1200) queued=320ms -> start
```
maria: ugh, looks like kernel selection is biasing toward the low-latency fastpath when short tokens dominate, which forces long reqs into a slow path later. did we flip the kernel-priority change last week? @sam
sam: yeah i pushed kernel selector change (prefer fastpath when avg_seq_len < 128) — intended to improve short tail. but didn't account for mixed-tenant KV pressure.
maria: that matches. good catch. think we need a batching heuristic tweak rather than revert. long churn is costly because of KV misses + rewarm.
ellie: can we try reserving slots or token-budgeting per-tenancy window? e.g. give long requests a small guaranteed admit token so they don't keep getting pushed back.
aj: proposed lightweight config to experiment (canary):
```yaml
batcher_config:
  admit_policy: windowed_reserve
  short_window_ms: 4
  long_window_ms: 22
  reserve:
    long_tokens: 512
    per_tenant_max_reserved: 2
kernel_selector:
  prefer_fastpath_threshold: 96  # lower threshold so fastpath less aggressive
```
aj: rationale: smaller threshold reduces pathological fastpath bias; reserve gives long requests breathing room to get KV warmups.
kai: +1 to canary. suggest 5% traffic for team-x and team-y where we saw worst regressions. also add metric: p99_kv_evictions/sec_by_tenant and p95_queue_delay_by_seq_len.
sam: also consider a soft prefill for long requests: if a long request is queued and we see N short requests in last M ms, synthesize a tiny prefill token to trigger KV warmup in parallel. low-cost but might reduce rewarm penalty.
maria: hmm prefill seems clever but tricky. need safety guard to avoid doubling token count. maybe cap to 32 tokens and only for tenants with high active cache affinity.
infra-bot: canary-deploy scheduled: batcher-config v2026-03-17-heuristic1 -> canary 5% at 2026-03-18T03:00:00Z by @kai
kai: i'll own the canary and collect the new metrics. ellie, can you add the dashboard panels for kv_evictions and queue_delay_by_len?
ellie: on it. will add a combine panel and an alert rule: spike in kv_evictions > 50% baseline for 5m -> page oncall.
aj: follow-ups: 1) run canary for 48h 2) collect p50/p95/p99 by seq_len buckets (0-32,33-128,129-512,>512) 3) capture kernel selection counts per batch shape 4) verify end-to-end latency regressions for small requests (shouldn't regress more than 5%)
maria: if this works we should add an automatic fallback: if kv_evictions increase >30% we revert kernel selector threshold.
sam: noted — will add a toggle flag so fallback is automatic.
kai: timeframe: start canary 12hrs from now, check after 6h and 24h. moving to #incidents if things blow up. :rocket:
aj: thanks team. saving profiler dump and will post a follow-up with graphs once canary emits data.
